analysis.title: What's Trending Across Credit (22 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Equities are tracking the 2018 playbook but credit is not yet. Since Oct 6, NDX is -19.8% and SPX -11.6% (about 86% and 59% of Q4'18 drawdowns), while CDX IG is +7bp and HY +52bp (about 21% and 31% of 2018 widening).
VIX closed at 35.9 and HY is about 35bp tight to where vol implies. A regression of CDX HY on VIX since Jan 2025 implies about +420bp versus about 385bp today, a 2-standard-deviation dislocation.

AI credit is pricing a different cycle. IG Tech widened 30bp since Oct 6 versus 16bp for IG and 7bp for CDX IG, and now trades 21bp wide of the IG index versus 21bp tight in May. ORCL is about 80bp wider than October tights.

AI financing supply is straining relative value. IG priced $78.6bn last week, taking November to a record $198bn, including a $40bn GPU financing with an A- secured tranche at +345bp, about 30bp inside HY. GIR estimates $545bn of AI project financing needs.

Cash IG is widening faster than CDX (16bp versus 7bp since Oct 6) but a 24bp Treasury rally cut IG yield-to-worst 14bp to 5.87% and delivered +0.84% weekly return. All-in yield buyers mask spread underperformance and secondary liquidity has worsened.
HY had its worst week of 2026. OAS widened 51bp to +367bp, about double the prior 2026 weekly high of 27bp, and YTD return flipped to -0.32%.
HY decompression is accelerating. CCC OAS is +1,174bp (widest since April 2025), up 188bp since Oct 6 versus +90bp for Bs and +44bp for BBs. CDX HY/IG ratio is only 5.9x, 18th percentile.

HY breadth is deteriorating. 65 bonds fell 5pts or more (24 the prior week), 45 of them BB or B. 90% of HY bonds declined and share inside +200bp fell 12.4pts to 44.5%. Four of ten HY deals broke issue after six weeks of every deal trading up.

Equity-credit dislocation is historically unusual. SPX -8.6% was a 4.9-sigma move versus 3.6 for CDX IG and 1.1 for CDX HY. Friday was the first VIX 30+ close since Jan 2025 with CDX HY inside +404bp and IG inside +66.5bp.

A full 2018 replay from Oct 6 implies about 27bp more IG widening and about 98bp in HY. The counterargument is that an AI slowdown could be benign for credit via lower capex, less supply and lower rates, though a broadening equity selloff weakens that.

Flows: equity HF net positioning at 3rd percentile over three years, CTAs sold $57bn of US equities in a month, GS Panic Index near 10/10. Macro and systematic accounts are buying CDX protection while real money is balanced. PT desk saw $29bn inquiry with HY clients buying 1.5:1.
Credit desk trade: IG47 Feb 65/80 payer spread versus 55 receiver seagull (16c) to play for wider spreads and hedge core longs. Desk view is credit bends but does not break in the AI unwind.

Equity desks see vol panic but positioning not fully washed out. HF beta-adjusted net leverage is 48.2% (five-year low), but sentiment is at 75th percentile, funds took in about $150-170bn, and futures positioning is at the 82nd percentile. Snider needs AI earnings confidence, a dovish Fed or washout to call a bottom.

Tech sell-off is a sentiment bear market. NDX -11% on the week, Semis -17% (worst since Sep 2011), NVDA -21%. Valuations are at 10-15 year lows (NDX 17x, SOX about 12-13x forward P/E) but there is no clear catalyst.
Dollar still has fight left. A hawkish US policy shock is feeding growth worries and moving dollar strength from DM to EM. GS expects only gradual softening in 2027 and likes COP and ZAR.
GIR 2027 credit outlook expects a maturing cycle, modest spread widening and below-median excess returns, preferring subordination premium over lower-rated credit.
Havens have behaved poorly in the selloff, with gold -10.8% and USDJPY +1.0% since Oct 6.

risk_factors: Credit catch-down to equity stress, with a 2018 replay implying about +27bp IG and +98bp HY.
Deteriorating secondary liquidity, especially in longer-duration IG.
AI financing supply competing with traditional corporate credit for capital.
HY breadth deterioration spreading from CCC to BB and single-B and into fins, cable, consumer finance.
Equity selloff broadening beyond tech, undermining the benign-AI-slowdown credit view.
Hawkish US policy shock feeding growth worries and EM FX weakness.
Equity positioning not fully washed out, with futures at the 82nd percentile.
vol_and_positioning: VIX closed at 35.9 and HY is about 35bp tight to vol-implied levels. Only 1.4% of observations since Jan 2025 show credit this tight relative to VIX.
GS Vol Panic Index is 9.8/10 and readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief. VXN is at its highest since COVID and VXSMH is at an all-time high.

6-week straddle more than doubled from 4% to 8.2%. Brian Garrett prefers long delta with net short or vega-flat footprint: window knock-outs, VIX calendar put spreads, and short puts in high-conviction longs.
Equity desk would sell puts in tech rather than chase delta and thinks a tactical entry is near.
HF beta-adjusted net leverage is 48.2%, a five-year low, and at the 1st-3rd percentile on a 3y view. CTAs flipped net short after selling $57bn in a month.
Macro and systematic accounts are buying CDX protection and downside convexity. HFs are pressing shorts in Tereos, Ineos and OI.
Single-stock shorting was the heaviest since Jun 2022 and HFs net sold for a third straight week.

tension_points.bull_case: Credit bends but does not break. CDX IG widened only about 6bp versus SPX -8.6%, inside its vol-implied beta, as an AI slowdown could lower capex, supply and rates, supporting debt serviceability.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit is 35bp tight to VIX-implied and has realized only 15% (IG) and 28% (HY) of 2018 widening while NDX has done about 70%. A full replay implies +27bp IG and +98bp HY.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further growth expectation deterioration as the equity selloff broadens beyond tech would undermine the benign credit view.

tension_points.bull_case: Vol panic index at 9.8/10 (above 9.5 has signaled near-term relief), HF nets at 1st-3rd percentile, valuations at 10-15 year lows, so a tactical entry is near.
tension_points.bear_case: Sentiment is still at the 75th percentile, futures positioning at the 82nd percentile and funds took in about $150-170bn, so positioning is not washed out and there is no clear catalyst.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A dovish Fed signal, more confidence in AI earnings or a positioning washout would be the confirming conditions, absent them the buyers' strike continues.
